claims: The exact-out canonical key is the lexicographic tuple `(input_total, leg_count, legs_lex)`.
The key ordering unfolds to input minimization, then fewer legs, then lexicographic leg ordering.
Every nonempty finite candidate key set has a unique canonical minimum.
A candidate is the canonical minimum exactly when it is in the set and no worse than every set element.
The canonical minimum exposes the intended exact-out tie-break priorities: minimal input, then fewer legs, then lexicographic legs.
proof_method: case analysis on the unfolded exact-out key order
